cases.customer_question: Can a Bluetooth module that references separate Host and Controller QDIDs be treated as a single Component registration for SIG qualification?
question_variants: Is this Bluetooth module a Component registration?
Why is the module treated as Multi-Design instead of Component?
Do we need to reference both Host and Controller QDIDs?
Can one Declaration ID represent a complete Component?
Why did the qualification support cost increase for this module?
cases.actual_issue: The customer believed the Bluetooth module was already registered as a Component, but the referenced Declaration actually consisted of separate Host Subsystem and Controller Subsystem QDIDs that had to be combined during qualification.
cases.plain_english_explanation: The Bluetooth module vendor indicated that the module could be treated as a Component registration, but the qualification review showed that the SIG records only contained separate Host and Controller subsystem references. Because the registration was not a single unified Component or End Product declaration, the product qualification had to reference multiple QDIDs together. This increased the qualification complexity and validation work.
cases.consultant_answer: The consultant explained that the referenced declaration consisted of separate Host Subsystem and Controller Subsystem QDIDs rather than a single Component or End Product registration. Because the qualification must combine multiple referenced designs, the registration falls under a Multi-Design workflow. The consultant further explained that after the 2024-07-01 SIG process changes, consistency checks between Controller and Host layers became stricter, increasing the amount of ICS correction and validation work required when combining multiple QDIDs.
cases.decision_logic: If a Bluetooth module qualification requires separate Host and Controller subsystem references rather than a single Component or End Product QDID, the product must be handled as a Multi-Design reference. Multi-QDID combinations require additional consistency validation between stack layers.
cases.final_recommendation: Verify whether the referenced Bluetooth declaration is truly a single Component or End Product registration. If separate Host and Controller subsystem QDIDs are required, plan the project as a Multi-Design qualification with additional consistency validation effort.
cases.risk_if_done_wrong: Incorrectly assuming that a module is a single Component registration can cause underestimation of qualification complexity, missing ICS consistency validation work, declaration errors, additional support effort, qualification delays, and incorrect project costing.
